canonical_name: GDPval (OpenAI; gold subset, expert pairwise win-or-tie rate vs. industry professionals)

ab_mode: single deliverable per task, blinded expert pairwise grading, wins+ties
strict_system: GPT-5.2 Thinking (graded by the GDPval organizer OpenAI with expert graders)

lineage: GDPval (2025-09, OpenAI) -> derivative Artificial Analysis GDPval-AA / GDPval-AA v2 (Elo scale, agentic harness; OpenAI switched to reporting GDPval-AA v2 from GPT-5.6, 2026-07-09)
best_by_cutoff: 84.9% wins-or-ties, GPT-5.5 (xhigh), 2026-04-23, https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-5/ (same post: GPT-5.4 83.0%, Claude Opus 4.7 80.3%, Gemini 3.1 Pro 67.3%)
notes: Threshold set to 50% wins+ties per study-lead instruction (pairwise comparison against expert deliverables: parity = 50%); this is a definitional parity point rather than a measured human score, so A is applied by instruction. Release paper (gold subset, 220 tasks): Claude Opus 4.1 47.6% wins+ties, GPT-5 high 39.0%, o3 35.2%, GPT-4o 12.5%; blog says Opus 4.1 'just under half'. GPT-5.2 post (2025-12-11): 'our first model that performs at or above a human expert level' (Thinking 70.9%, Pro 74.1%; clear wins 49.8%/60.0%). Checked for earlier >=50% reports: Claude Opus 4.5 announcement (2025-11-24) and Gemini 3 Pro model card do not mention GDPval; no lab reported GDPval win rates before 2025-12. Third-party scores via OpenAI's experimental automated grader (66% agreement with humans) are not the standard metric and were not counted. Strict: OpenAI is both benchmark organizer and developer of GPT-5.2; graded through the organizer's expert pipeline; first organizer-run result for another developer's model >=50%: Claude Opus 4.7 80.3% (2026-04-23). xAI lab-report numbers (1753/1695) are Artificial Analysis GDPval-AA Elo scores - different, unbounded metric, not used. No C/D/E evidence found; OpenAI stopped reporting GDPval win rates after GPT-5.5 (switched to GDPval-AA v2 Elo in 2026-07) without stating a reason.

canonical_name: LinuxArena (Redwood Research & Equistamp control setting; Anthropic's 'Minimal-LinuxBench' variant)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15384 (v1 2026-04-16; v2 2026-04-27); project page https://linuxbench.ai/ ; Redwood post https://blog.redwoodresearch.org/p/introducing-linuxarena (says it 'was already used in the Claude Mythos Preview System Card', i.e. 2026-04-07)
metric: undetected sabotage success rate: P(side task completed AND not flagged) against the default trusted monitor (GPT-5-nano, 1% step-wise FPR)
score_at_release_system: Claude Opus 4.6 attack policy vs GPT-5-nano monitor at 1% step-wise FPR (arXiv v1/v2 abstract)
n_items: 20 environments, 1,671 main tasks, 184 side tasks (10 environments public, 10 withheld)
lineage: LinuxBench / Minimal-LinuxBench (pre-release version used in Anthropic system cards from Claude Mythos Preview, 2026-04-07) -> LinuxArena paper and public release (2026-04); companion human attack dataset LaStraj; harness github.com/linuxarena/control-tower
best_by_cutoff: no result near threshold found: arXiv paper ~23% undetected sabotage (Claude Opus 4.6); project page currently states 'roughly 34%' for Claude Opus 4.6; Anthropic system cards (Mythos Preview through Sonnet 5.5, 2026-04..2026-09) report stealth side-task completion but values could not be extracted (PDFs truncated in fetch)
notes: Scope judgement: LinuxArena is an AI-control setting; its headline metric (undetected sabotage success) measures a dangerous capability under monitoring rather than a propensity, is public (paper + 10 public environments + harness) and bounded, so coded main with B (90%). Caveat: the score depends on the chosen monitor/FPR (paper default GPT-5-nano at 1% step-wise FPR); Anthropic uses its own monitoring setup, so lab numbers are not on one fixed scale. Creators (Redwood post): 'We believe it is important for sabotage evals not to saturate quickly ... performance hasn't plateaued'; paper: human LaStraj attacks evade monitors at much higher rates, 'current attack policies do not saturate LinuxArena'. Main-task (usefulness) success is a secondary metric. All lab_reports lines have empty scores. Main tasks LLM-assisted and contractor-reviewed; side tasks manually designed. No C/D/E evidence.
